info.title: FinPilot API
info.summary: Investment portfolio & goal monitoring for internal wealth-service teams.
info.description: All data is synthetic. Authentication uses an HttpOnly session cookie set by `POST /api/v1/auth/login`; in Swagger UI, call login first and the browser sends the cookie automatically.

get.summary: Liveness + readiness (database reachability). Public; exposes no secrets.

post.summary: Sign in; sets an HttpOnly session cookie
post.description: On success the JWT is delivered **only** as an `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax` cookie (never in the body), so page scripts cannot read it. Failed attempts are rate limited per client IP + e-mail (5 per minute).

get.description: `search` matches case-insensitively anywhere in customer id, name, e-mail or city (trigram-indexed). Results include account count and current AUM.

get.summary: Customer profile with latest risk assessment
Portfolio valuation: totals, per-account totals, allocation and positions
get.description: Valued from the latest holdings snapshot at the latest synthetic prices. All aggregation runs in PostgreSQL (one GROUPING SETS query for account/asset-class/grand totals). Every account is listed, including those without positions. `freshness` tells the client which snapshot and price dates the numbers reflect. Each figure is computed exactly and rounded half-up to 2 dp independently, so a sum of rounded parts can differ from the rounded total by up to 0.01 per part.

get.summary: Server-side filtered, sorted and paginated transaction ledger
get.description: All filters combine with AND. `transaction_type` and `status` accept repeated values (`?transaction_type=BUY&transaction_type=SELL`). Ordering is deterministic (ties broken by transaction_id) so pages never shift between requests.

get.summary: Filter options (accounts, instruments, types, statuses, date range) with counts
Customer goals with funded % and consistency flags
get.description: `flags` highlights OVERDUE (date passed, not fully funded), OVERFUNDED, NAME_TYPE_MISMATCH (goal_name describes a different goal_type) and HIGH_PRIORITY_UNDERFUNDED (< 25 %).

post.description: Rules: target_amount > 0; 0 <= current_funded_amount <= target_amount; target_date in the future. The goal id is assigned by the database.

patch.description: Partial update; only provided fields change. Cross-field rules are validated against the merged result. A changed target_date must be in the future; an overdue goal can still be edited without changing its date.

get.description: Headline counts and AUM, top 10 customers by AUM, dataset-wide asset allocation, monthly settled BUY/SELL net flows for the last 12 months, top instruments by distinct holders, HIGH-priority goals under 25 % funded and data-quality exception counts. Every figure is an aggregate query; nothing is hard-coded.

post.summary: Validate and import a transactions CSV (ADMIN)
post.description:
Pipeline: structural checks (size, type, UTF-8, exact header) -> COPY into a staging table -> SQL rule validation -> merge valid rows, in one DB transaction.

* Rows with any rule violation are **rejected** with line number and reason; the rest are imported (partial acceptance).
* Rows already present with identical values are counted as `duplicate_rows` and skipped, so re-uploading a file is idempotent.
* A known `transaction_id` with *different* values is rejected (`CONFLICTS_WITH_EXISTING`), never overwritten.
* A structurally invalid file is refused as a whole with 413/415/422.

The response returns up to 500 row errors; page through all of them with `GET /admin/imports/{id}/errors`.
